answer: DeepWalk uses short random walks on the graph as its input, treating the resulting vertex sequences like sentences. The learned latent representation encodes local neighborhood structure and broader graph proximity/co-occurrence patterns, so vertices that appear in similar random-walk contexts get similar embeddings.
confidence_reasoning: This is a well-established description of DeepWalk and matches the original method: random-walk vertex sequences are used to learn embeddings that preserve graph neighborhood/co-occurrence information.
